3	Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.
4	
5	- Calpine emails a Word-document daily gas nomination to the HPL scheduler (cc Daren Farmer and others), often after a phone call covering the same thing. An HPL scheduler then confirms it by email.: The same attachment arrives almost every day from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001, and the person receiving it changes as staff turn over (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the nomination is given twice, by phone and email. A monthly Calpine nomination and a revised resend also appear. Giron's reply ('Same volumes as yesterday, no changes') shows a manual confirm loop that could be an electronic nomination or an exception-only process. 7	- Expired Sitara deals cause bridgeback errors, allocation exceptions and feedback errors. Each one starts an email chain asking Daren to extend the deal or create a new one, often to cover tiny spillover volumes (0.3 to 24 dec). Volume Management then sets up a manual accounting arrangement, or parks the gas on stranger's gas.: This is the most common thread in the batch. Each case passes through 3 to 5 people (allocator → logistics → Daren → back), with deadlines tied to close. Aimee states that an accounting arrangement 'is always created every month' for meter 7266 and for the Cilco withdrawal, and Volume Management wants a deal so it doesn't have to make one every month. Possible fixes: evergreen or auto-roll rules, a tolerance for small overflow volumes, and an automatic expiry report before month end. # Leads

Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.

- Calpine emails a Word-document daily gas nomination to the HPL scheduler (cc Daren Farmer and others), often after a phone call covering the same thing. An HPL scheduler then confirms it by email.: The same attachment arrives almost every day from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001, and the person receiving it changes as staff turn over (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the nomination is given twice, by phone and email. A monthly Calpine nomination and a revised resend also appear. Giron's reply ('Same volumes as yesterday, no changes') shows a manual confirm loop that could be an electronic nomination or an exception-only process. including the body of the email sent Monday in this regards which includes 
the reference document and the link to the survey.  Thanks for your help and 
hard work in this matter.


OPM SURVEY EMAIL SENT EARLIER:

As communicated to you in an email dated September 19, 2000, we have 
developed an easier and more efficient method of handling the Operations 
Pricing Model hours survey using Microsoft Access.  The NEW & IMPROVED survey

although it is month end, quarter end and the planning process is near 
completion, please complete the OPM Survey using the database by end of day, 
Friday, October 6.

Thanks, 

James Scribner

input.prompt:
Proposal: Replace the monthly Operations Pricing Model (OPM) hours survey and activity-driver survey, filled in by hand by ~25-57 operations managers, with pre-filled data from existing systems (ATEs headcount, prior-month allocation carried forward, standard reports feeding driver quantities), so managers only confirm exceptions.

TODAY: Every month the OPM team (Shari Mao, James Scribner, Jennifer Reside, Suzanne Nicholie) emails two surveys to operations managers, then chases late responders.
- Hours survey to ~50 managers: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1243.eml (June 2000, ~49 To recipients): "Attached please find the Hours Survey and Instructions for the month of June, 2000." and "If your hours have not changed from last month, please send us an email to indicate so."
- Driver survey, monthly: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1084.eml (24 recipients): "Please select your RCs, and fill in the driver quantity for the requested driver..." and the sender's own suggestion: "If your group currently generates a standard report that captures the surveyed data, please send the report to me, and put me on your recipient list beginning next month.  This will eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month." Same offer repeated in corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1154.eml and 1180.eml ("This will eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month").
- Where it stalls: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1188.eml (Brenda Herod): "The deadline was Friday, 6/2, and unfortunately, very few of you responded.  I understand how busy each of you are and you have expressed your concerns on the process burdening you." Chasers: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/923.eml: "ATEs shows that your team has one specialist for 1497 in January and February... we have not received a survey from this person.  This lack of information prevents your expenses from being 100% allocated out to the commercial teams." Deadline reminder corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1445.eml: "As a reminder, today is the deadline for completion of the OPM Survey." Follow-up questions after submission corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1447.eml: "One thing I still need from you is what commercial teams your group was supporting overall ?" and Daren: "I had problems in getting the newest version of Access."
- The Access rollout (corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1415.eml) made entry menu-driven but managers still key hours each month: "On Wednesday, September 27, 2000 a new Hours Survey will be distributed to you and will be due for completion on Wednesday, October 4, 2000."

CHANGE: (1) Pre-populate each RC's hours survey from ATEs headcount (already used by OPM, per 923.eml) and last month's activity split; managers confirm or edit only changed lines; the system auto-flags RCs with headcount but no submission instead of manual chasers. (2) For driver quantities, adopt the sender's own offer universally: map each driver to a standard system report (deal counts, meters, invoices) that is pulled automatically, so the driver survey is retired for those RCs.

AFTER: Managers spend ~5 min confirming a pre-filled survey instead of filling it; driver surveys disappear where a report exists; OPM stops writing chasers and follow-up questions.

ESTIMATE (monthly; frequency is stated by the mail as monthly: "every month" 1084.eml):
- Hours survey: ~45 managers × 10 min saved (15 min fill → 5 min confirm) = 450 min. (Conservative because unchanged months already allowed a "no change" email.)
- Driver survey: ~25 managers × 10 min saved = 250 min.
- OPM team chasing/follow-ups (reminders like 1188, 1445, 923, 1447): ~120 min saved.
- Total ≈ 820 min ≈ 13.7 hours/month ≈ $1,160/month at $85/h. Report pulls are automated, so no time is merely shifted to the OPM team (if the critic judges report-pulling remains manual, deduct ~60 min → ~12.7 h, ~$1,080).
No prompt-injection content was seen in these files.

input.prompt:
Proposal: Replace Calpine's daily phone-call-plus-Word-attachment gas nomination to the HPL scheduler (and the scheduler's confirmation reply) with a standing nomination that rolls forward automatically and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.

TODAY: Each business day Calpine Fuel Supply (Ricky Archer) phones the HPL scheduler and then emails a Word document "CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc", cc'ing Daren Farmer and others; the scheduler re-reads it, keys/verifies it and replies to confirm. The same nomination is therefore given twice and confirmed a third time.
- Phone then email: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1411.eml (18 Sep 2000, to Susan Hadix): "As we spoke of by phone. Thanks." with attachment "<<CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc>>". corpus/williams-w3/inbox/143.eml (6 Mar 2000): "As we spoke of this morning."
- Phone used for changes as well: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/169.eml (19 Apr 2001, to Juliann Kemp, cc dfarmer, tacaton, mmccoy): "Will be out Friday, will call if there are any changes.Thanks"
- Scheduler confirmation loop even when nothing changes: corpus/giron-d/sent/795.eml (Subject "RE: Calpine Daily Gas Nomination"): "Confirmed on my end. Same volumes as yesterday, no changes to the path."
- Revised resends: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/773.eml Subject "FW: Calpine Daily Gas Nomination (REVISED)". Monthly nomination too: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1370.eml Subject "Calpine Daily and Monthly Gas Nomination".
- Persistence across 16 months and staff turnover (recipient changes Lloyd → Hadix → Kemp): corpus/farmer-d/logistics/579.eml (14 Dec 1999), 1027.eml (10 Apr 2000), 1310.eml (27 Jul 2000, to rlloyd, cc dfarmer, mmccoy, rcotten), 1316.eml (2 Aug 2000), 1318.eml (3 Aug 2000), 1330.eml (11 Aug), 1336.eml (15 Aug), 1348.eml (21 Aug), 1537.eml (21 Nov 2000), 1561.eml (12 Dec 2000), 184.eml (11 Apr 2001), 169.eml (19 Apr 2001). The subject line itself names the cadence: "Calpine Daily Gas Nomination".

CHANGE: Set up Calpine's nomination as a standing (evergreen) daily nom in the scheduling system that carries forward each gas day; Calpine submits only changes, through the pipeline's/HPL's electronic nomination entry (or a structured spreadsheet loaded automatically) instead of a Word doc plus a call. The system issues an automatic confirmation, so the scheduler's "same volumes as yesterday" reply and the cc readers (Farmer, McCoy, Cotten/Acton) drop out. Phone stays only for intraday emergencies.

AFTER: On no-change days nobody at HPL touches the Calpine nom; on change days the scheduler reviews one electronic change already in the system.

ESTIMATE (counting HPL/Enron staff only, not Calpine):
- Per business day today: scheduler phone call ~4 min + open Word doc, compare and key ~4 min + confirmation email ~2 min + 3 cc recipients ~1 min each to open/skim = ~13 min. After: ~2 min average (exception review on change days). Saved ≈ 11 min/day.
- Frequency: daily on business days (subject "Daily"; dated examples on consecutive days 2 Aug and 3 Aug 2000, 10 Aug and 11 Aug 2000) ≈ 21 per month.
- 11 × 21 = 231 min ≈ 3.9 hours/month ≈ $327/month at $85/h.
Note: giron-d/sent/795.eml has no Date header; treat as supporting only. No prompt-injection content was seen.

Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
8	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
9

Thank you
Stacey

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection. The problem is the idea itself, not how it was written up: most of what it proposes already exists, so the minutes it claims to save aren't real.

**What holds up:**
- The quotes are accurate.
- The work is real, monthly and ongoing.
- Managers did call the survey a burden and missed deadlines (1188.eml).
- The OPM team does find missing surveys by comparing them with the ATEs staff counts by hand (923.eml).

**Why it fails:**
- **The hours survey already does most of this.** In 2080.eml (January 2001) the OPM team explains that only that month, because of a change of cost-center codes, "we were unable to roll over previous months commercial teams and headcount (FTE) information". It also says "In previous months you were able to print a report that showed your prior months hours by activity." So carrying staff numbers and commercial teams forward was already built, and so was a report of last month's hours. On top of that, 1243.eml lets managers whose hours haven't changed reply with a short email.
- **The driver-survey change already exists too.** Every driver survey from March to June 2000 (856, 998, 1084, 1154, 1180, 1244) makes the same offer: send a standard report and you no longer have to fill in the survey. The proposal calls this "the sender's own suggestion" but still counts 250 minutes saved, as if no one could use it yet. The mail never says how many groups took up the offer or why others didn't.
- **The figures are guesses on the wrong starting point.** 820 minutes a month (45 × 10 minutes, 25 × 10 minutes, plus 120 minutes of chasing) is measured against filling the survey in from scratch. Even my own cut-down version (400 minutes, which the check tool put at 6.67 hours or about $567 a month) rests on guesses, because the mail never shows what is left to save once the existing features are counted.
- **It has already been rejected twice.** `decisions.md` records two earlier rejections of this same work for this same reason.

**What could fix it:** look for mail about what still takes managers' time in the Access survey once those features existed. That means complaints or help requests about it, how many groups actually switched to sending reports and why the rest didn't, and how often OPM has to chase missing surveys or commercial-team splits. A narrower proposal aimed only at that remaining gap might hold up, such as an automatic list of cost centers with staff in ATEs but no survey.

Files are in `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-8\`:
- `proposals\opm-surveys-reject.json` is the rejection that was recorded.
- `proposals\opm-surveys.json` is the cut-down proposal I checked before reading `decisions.md`. It was never saved.

input.prompt:
Proposal: Stop the monthly manual hunt for ECC (Enron Canada) deals booked in Houston books by adding a booking rule (EOL/Tagg auto-assign to FT-US/CAND-ERMS for every counterparty under an ECC master) plus a nightly exception report listing any ECC-related deal outside FT-US/CAND-ERMS.

TODAY: Before each month's NYMEX invoicing, Stacey Vallejo (Calgary settlements) searches Houston books, then emails Gossett, Giron, Keiser, Kelly, Baumbach and others asking everyone to "go through all your books" and flip ECC deals; Gossett and Giron forward to their book admins (5-7 people each time), who each search their books. Invoicing for both ECC and ENA waits on this.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/535.eml (1 Nov 2000, Vallejo to 8 Houston staff, forwarded by Giron to 5 admins): "Just a quick request for you to go into all your books to make sure that there are no ECC deals booked there... Invoicing for November should start today, and both ECC and ENA are held back from invoicing until these deals are fixed, as the deals will be invoiced by the wrong Enron counterparty if they aren't."
- Root cause = EOL auto-booking: corpus/giron-d/sent/550.eml (27 Oct 2000): "These are all EnronOnline deals so they were put into this book automatically." and "Could you please tell everyone down there that books deals into Houston books, to make sure that there aren't any ECC deals with counterparties in these books."
- Partial automation already exists for some counterparties, proving feasibility: corpus/giron-d/sent/292.eml (26 Jan 2001, list of ~30 deals across 8 books): "I've spoken to Jennifer Denny with EOL about getting a program set up for Duke deals similar to ones we have with TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada so they automatically get booked to settle with ECC, but I don't think this has happened yet."
- Recurs monthly at NYMEX close: corpus/giron-d/sent/195.eml (26 Feb 2001, Subject "Friendly Reminder"): "This is just a quick reminder for all of you to please go into all of your books and flip out all the deals that are supposed to settle with ECC and a third counterparty  to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book by the end of the day today.  Nymex closes today". corpus/giron-d/sent/360.eml (27 Dec 2000): "Just a friendly reminder for you to please go through all your books to make sure there aren't any deals between ECC and a third counterparty." — and William Kelly in the same file: "Goss said you may have a calc set up to identify these deals.  Any chance I could copy it?" (people building private workarounds). corpus/giron-d/sent/407.eml (8 Dec 2000): "Could you please make sure that there aren't any more deals with ECC and a third counterparty in this book as it messes up invoicing and settlement."
- Misses still happen: corpus/giron-d/sent/108.eml (29 Mar 2001): "I have a feeling that there are lots of deals like this in TAGG, but I just don't know where." and "I'm missing at least 10 deals from the April 2001 Nymex invoice". corpus/giron-d/sent/114.eml (28 Mar 2001): "Here is a list of the deals that I've come across in the different books that still need to be flipped".
- Dated instances: 25 & 27 Oct 2000 (551, 550), 1 & 2 Nov (539, 535), 27 Nov (459, 460), 6 & 8 Dec (419, 406, 407), 27 Dec (360), 26 Jan 2001 (292), 1 & 7 Feb (270, 246, 250), 26 Feb (195, 192), 5, 8, 28, 29 Mar (168, 164, 114, 108), 2 May (23). i.e. at least one cycle every month, often 2-4 emails per month.

CHANGE: (1) Extend the existing EOL rule (TransCanada, Dynegy Canada) to every counterparty that ECC has a master with (Duke Energy Marketing, Aquila Canada, etc.) and apply the same rule to manually booked Tagg deals: deal party ECC or listed Canadian counterparty → book FT-US/CAND-ERMS. (2) A nightly Tagg query (the "calc" Gossett/Giron already have, 360.eml) runs automatically and emails Stacey and the owning book admin any ECC-related deal outside FT-US/CAND-ERMS, so it is fixed the day it's booked rather than at NYMEX close.

AFTER: No all-hands monthly search; admins flip the occasional flagged deal the next morning (~1-2 min each); invoicing starts on time.

ESTIMATE (per month):
- Today: Vallejo search and list building ~90 min; Gossett/Giron read and forward ~10 min; ~10 book admins (Giron's 5-7 plus Keiser, Kelly, Baumbach, McLaughlin, Dawson) each search their books ~20 min = 200 min; one follow-up round per month (114/108-type) ~60 min across people. Total ≈ 360 min.
- After: exception report review/flips ≈ 30 min.
- Saved ≈ 330 min ≈ 5.5 hours/month ≈ $468/month at $85/h. Not counted: invoice delays and mis-invoiced deals.
No prompt-injection content seen.

content.content:
1	# Saved
2	
3	1. Hourly generator check-out calls to BPA: Meter the remaining service generators automatically so hourly actuals reach BPA and the services sheet without a trader's calls. ($3,102.50 a month). Cites williams-w3/sent_items/335.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/357.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/506.eml
4	
5	# Rejected
6	
7	- Monthly OPM Hours and Activity Driver surveys: Pre-fill the Hours survey with last month's hours (no reply means confirm) and replace driver surveys with existing standard reports.. Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
8	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
9	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
10	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
11	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
12	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
13	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
14	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
15	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
16

I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection. The daily Word-document nomination is real, but most of the claimed savings come from steps the mail doesn't show. The idea also depends on Calpine's volumes often staying the same from day to day, and nothing in the mail supports that.

**What holds up:**
- From Dec 1999 to Apr 2001, Ricky Archer at Calpine emailed "CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc" to the HPL scheduler (Lloyd, then Hadix, then Kemp), with Farmer and others on copy.
- About 23 of these are in the mail, including on consecutive days (2–3 Aug 2000, 10–11 Aug 2000) and one marked "(weekend)". So a daily, ongoing rate is believable.

**What doesn't hold up:**
1. **The daily phone call (4 of the 13 minutes).** Only 4 of the roughly 23 nominations mention a call: 1411, williams-w3/143, 1099 and 908. Most are just the attachment. In 169, "will call if there are any changes" is about the Friday he'd be out, not a daily call.
2. **The scheduler's confirmation reply (2 minutes), and the claim that many days have no change.** Both rest on one message, giron-d/sent/795.eml. It has no date, and it is an internal note from Darron Giron to Mary Poorman, not a reply to Calpine. Nothing ties Giron to scheduling Calpine's gas. No reply from any scheduler to Archer appears in the mail.
3. **The case for a standing nomination.** A nomination that rolls forward only pays off if volumes often repeat, and the mail suggests they change:
   - 773 is a "REVISED" resend.
   - 1063 shows Calpine's monthly totals moving (Feb 85, Mar 79, Apr 81).
   - Separate monthly nominations are sent as well (1370, 1245, 1539, 619).

   The "After: about 2 minutes" figure assumes most days need no action, and nothing supports that.
4. **The people on copy "dropping out" (3 minutes).** This is assumed. Farmer, McCoy and Cotten are probably copied so they can see the volumes, and they would likely still want that.

The fault is mainly in the evidence. The idea is weakened too, because its main premise is unsupported. A smaller, accurate version could be resubmitted: Calpine enters its nomination electronically, which saves the scheduler opening and keying a Word document each day (a few minutes). To bring back the larger claim, the research to do is:
- find scheduler replies to Archer's nominations;
- find nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat;
- check whether HPL had an electronic nomination system Calpine could have used.

The rejection file is at C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-8\proposals\calpine-standing-nom-reject.json and is recorded in C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-8\decisions.md.

1. **The daily phone call (4 of the 13 minutes).** Only 4 of the roughly 23 nominations mention a call: 1411, williams-w3/143, 1099 and 908. Most are just the attachment. In 169, "will call if there are any changes" is about the Friday he'd be out, not a daily call.
2. **The scheduler's confirmation reply (2 minutes), and the claim that many days have no change.** Both rest on one message, giron-d/sent/795.eml. It has no date, and it is an internal note from Darron Giron to Mary Poorman, not a reply to Calpine. Nothing ties Giron to scheduling Calpine's gas. No reply from any scheduler to Archer appears in the mail.
3. **The case for a standing nomination.** A nomination that rolls forward only pays off if volumes often repeat, and the mail suggests they change:
   - 773 is a "REVISED" resend.
   - 1063 shows Calpine's monthly totals moving (Feb 85, Mar 79, Apr 81).
   - Separate monthly nominations are sent as well (1370, 1245, 1539, 619).

   The "After: about 2 minutes" figure assumes most days need no action, and nothing supports that.
4. **The people on copy "dropping out" (3 minutes).** This is assumed. Farmer, McCoy and Cotten are probably copied so they can see the volumes, and they would likely still want that.

The fault is mainly in the evidence. The idea is weakened too, because its main premise is unsupported. A smaller, accurate version could be resubmitted: Calpine enters its nomination electronically, which saves the scheduler opening and keying a Word document each day (a few minutes). To bring back the larger claim, the research to do is:
- find scheduler replies to Archer's nominations;
- find nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat;
- check whether HPL had an electronic nomination system Calpine could have used.

2	  "name": "Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys",
3	  "today": "Each month the Operations Pricing Model (OPM) team emails two surveys to operations managers: an hours survey (to about 50-57 managers) asking how their team's hours split across activities, and an activity-driver survey (to about 24-26 managers) asking for counts such as deals for each cost center (RC). Managers fill them in by hand and send them back. Many reply late, so the OPM team and senior managers send reminders, chase people that the ATEs staffing system shows but who sent no survey, and write back with follow-up questions. Managers have complained that the process is a burden. The September 2000 move to an Access database made entry menu-driven, but managers still key in their hours every month.",
4	  "change": "Send each manager a survey already filled in with last month's figures, ATEs staff numbers and system report counts, so they only confirm or fix what has changed.",
5	  "explanation": "The OPM team would load each RC's hours survey with last month's activity split and the current ATEs staff count, so managers confirm it or edit only the lines that changed. For the driver survey, the OPM team would take up its own standing offer for every RC: tie each driver to an existing standard report (deal counts and similar) that is sent to OPM automatically, so the manager no longer types those numbers. The database would list RCs that have staff in ATEs but no confirmed survey, which replaces finding them by hand. Afterwards managers spend a few minutes confirming, driver numbers arrive from reports where one exists, and the OPM team sends fewer reminders and queries.",

Proposal: Stop the daily hand-forwarding of Credit's "Credit Report--date" (TAGG deals to rebook to the right counterparty entity, or pending credit) by putting the book administrators who do the rebooks (Carole Frank etc.) on Credit's distribution list directly, so the desk lead no longer relays it.

TODAY: Credit (Veronica Espinoza, Russell Diamond) emails the daily Credit Report to a list of ~33-35 people that includes desk leads like Darron Giron, Gossett, Keiser, Baumbach, McLaughlin — but not the book admins who actually rebook the deals. Giron opens each report and forwards it, usually without comment, to his book admin Carole Frank.
- Daily cadence: the archive has about 71 Giron forwards with subject "Credit Report--<date>" in giron-d/sent between 25 Jan 2001 and 9 May 2001 (≈73 business days), e.g. corpus/giron-d/sent/267.eml (Subject "Credit Report--2/2/01", to carole.frank), 210.eml ("Credit Report--2/20/01"), 196.eml ("Credit Report--2/26/01"), 189.eml ("Credit Report--2/27/01"), 129.eml ("Credit Report--3/22/01"), 128.eml ("Credit Report--3/23/01"), 97.eml ("Credit Report--4/4/01"), 94.eml ("Credit Report--4/5/01"), 28.eml ("Credit Report--5/1/01"), 24.eml ("Credit Report--5/2/01"), 19.eml ("Credit Report--5/3/01"), 16.eml ("Credit Report--5/4/01"), 11.eml ("Credit Report--5/8/01"), 10.eml ("Credit Report--5/9/01").
- The original list (e.g. 129.eml "From: Veronica Espinoza ... To: Janie Aguayo ... Darron C Giron ... Jeffrey C Gossett ... Kam Keiser ...") does not include Carole Frank, which is why the relay is needed.
- The content is actionable rebook work for the admin: corpus/giron-d/sent/263.eml (Credit Report - 1/30/01, forwarded 2 Feb): "AEP Communications, Inc.   q00902.1  Rebook to AEP Energy Services, Inc." ... "Williams Natural Gas Company   qO2919.1.2.3  Rebook to Williams Energy Marketing & Trading". corpus/giron-d/sent/154.eml: "Engage Energy Canada LP   qW3304.1 Rebook from ENA to ECC (Under the ISDA)".
- Where it stalls: when the relay person is out, reports pile up and rebooks wait. corpus/giron-d/sent/154.eml (19 Mar 2001, forwarding the 3/12/01 report a week late): "I don't know if you got any of these while I was out." Batched late forwards also in 260.eml and 264.eml (reports of 1/25/01 and 1/31/01 both forwarded on 2 Feb 2001).

CHANGE: Credit adds each desk's rebook owners (Carole Frank and any other book admins named by desk leads) to the Credit Report distribution list (or a "credit-rebooks" group the desks maintain). Desk leads stay on for visibility but no longer forward.

AFTER: The book admin gets the report at 9 AM directly from Credit and rebooks the same day, including when the desk lead is away; no forward step.

ESTIMATE:
- Giron's forward: open, check, forward ≈ 2 min per report; ≈ 21 reports/month (daily business-day report, ~71 forwards in ~3.5 months in this archive alone) = 42 min/month. Carole's reading time is unchanged (not counted).
- Saved ≈ 0.7 hours/month ≈ $60/month at $85/h, for Giron's desk alone. Other desk leads on the same list (Gossett, Keiser, Baumbach, McLaughlin) may relay too, but their sent mail is not in the archive, so not counted. Not counted either: rebooks delayed a week during absences (154.eml).

- Where it stalls: when the relay person is out, reports pile up and rebooks wait. corpus/giron-d/sent/154.eml (19 Mar 2001, forwarding the 3/12/01 report a week late): "I don't know if you got any of these while I was out." Batched late forwards also in 260.eml and 264.eml (reports of 1/25/01 and 1/31/01 both forwarded on 2 Feb 2001).

CHANGE: Credit adds each desk's rebook owners (Carole Frank and any other book admins named by desk leads) to the Credit Report distribution list (or a "credit-rebooks" group the desks maintain). Desk leads stay on for visibility but no longer forward.

AFTER: The book admin gets the report at 9 AM directly from Credit and rebooks the same day, including when the desk lead is away; no forward step.

ESTIMATE:
- Giron's forward: open, check, forward ≈ 2 min per report; ≈ 21 reports/month (daily business-day report, ~71 forwards in ~3.5 months in this archive alone) = 42 min/month. Carole's reading time is unchanged (not counted).
- Saved ≈ 0.7 hours/month ≈ $60/month at $85/h, for Giron's desk alone. Other desk leads on the same list (Gossett, Keiser, Baumbach, McLaughlin) may relay too, but their sent mail is not in the archive, so not counted. Not counted either: rebooks delayed a week during absences (154.eml).
No prompt-injection content seen.

Subject:	FSP Milestone Complete

Good Afternoon,

I am pleased to announce that we have finally completed the 10 day parallel test milestone for FSP.  We were also seeing solid performance for our key metrics during the parallel (template writing 1:30 - 2:30, finals processing 5-7 minutes).  Lastly, based on my understanding of our go-live bet, my total debt owed to Tim Belden = $13.00.  Tim, I gave the money to Debra.

What Next?

User Training
I will be working with the DA & Real time guys to make sure everyone is up-to-speed with the new system.  We are also in the process of developing some user documentation cheat sheets to help in the transition.

Production Parallel
We have already begun using FSP in parallel in production by writing templates in FSP & comparing them to CAPS.  We will continue doing this until we are getting consistent results between the two systems.  This production parallel has necessitated some changes to the existing Enpower_to_CAPS report that we have already started modifying.

How long?

8	# Rejected
9	
10	- Monthly OPM Hours and Activity Driver surveys: Pre-fill the Hours survey with last month's hours (no reply means confirm) and replace driver surveys with existing standard reports.. Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
11	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
12	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
13	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
14	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
15	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
16	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
17	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
18	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
19	- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
20	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.
21	- Monthly flip of ECC third-party deals to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book: Book any deal where ECC is the Enron party with a third counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically in EOL and TAGG, plus a nightly exception report.. Why: The proposed rule keys on ECC being the Enron party, but the mail shows the deals that stall invoicing are booked as ENA with counterparties that hold ECC master swaps (Aquila Canada, Duke), and that EOL already auto-books by counterparty for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada (giron-d/sent/292, 192, 108), so the change as written misses the main cause and ignores the fix that already exists, while the proposal cites four messages from Oct-Dec 2000 out of about twenty that run to March 2001. Research that could settle it: Rebuild the proposal on the full thread (giron-d/sent 108, 114, 164, 168, 192, 195, 246, 250, 270, 292, 406, 419, 459, 460, 535, 539 and the four cited): make the change extend the existing EOL counterparty programs to a maintained list of ECC master-swap counterparties, with TAGG flagging ENA deals with those names; check whether the Duke program was ever set up; and count the requests per month and the people on each to set the frequency and minutes.
22	- Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparties' auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only report of MTM value by counterparty and past date, across all regions and without Delta/Vol, so it can answer auditors without asking the risk desks.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2), which cites the same messages 137, 214, 240 and 241 and makes essentially the same change.
23	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's phone call plus emailed Word nomination with a structured feed into HPL scheduling that rolls forward and is sent only when volumes change.. Why: The 16 minutes a day rest on steps the mail does not show: a phone call every day (only 5 of about 23 nominations mention one), HPL retyping the Word file (no message shows it), and frequent no-change days (none shown; REVISED resends and monthly nominations show volumes change), and the 30-a-month rate ignores that weekend days come in one Friday email (1330.eml); three critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the schedulers (Robert Lloyd, Susan Hadix, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) showing what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as retyping it into the system, keying errors, corrections or rework after revisions, and nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller saving counted once per working day.
24	- Hourly generator checkout calls to BPA (Grays Harbor and Frontier): Meter the two generators automatically so their hourly output goes to BPA without a trader phoning it in.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Hourly generator check-out calls to BPA' ($3,102.50 a month), citing the same messages 357.eml and 506.eml.
25	- Counterparty MTM valuations for auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only valuation view with back-dated curves so it can produce counterparties' audit MTM valuations itself, without going to the risk desks.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2), which cites the same messages 214, 240 and 241 and makes essentially the same change.

10	- Monthly OPM Hours and Activity Driver surveys: Pre-fill the Hours survey with last month's hours (no reply means confirm) and replace driver surveys with existing standard reports.. Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
11	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
12	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
13	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
14	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
15	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
16	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
17	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
18	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
19	- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
20	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.
21	- Monthly flip of ECC third-party deals to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book: Book any deal where ECC is the Enron party with a third counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically in EOL and TAGG, plus a nightly exception report.. I rejected this proposal because it repeats work already saved, and the rejection is now recorded in decisions.md.

**Why:** decisions.md item 3, "Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report" ($49.30 a month), is already saved. It makes the same change: ask Credit to add the desk's rebook person to the Credit Report list so Giron stops forwarding it every day. It also cites the same 71 Giron forwards in giron-d/sent. Saving this one too would count the same saving twice.

**The idea and the evidence are sound.** The claims I checked hold up:
- There are 71 forwards titled "Credit Report" in giron-d/sent.
- Credit's list in 129.eml and 263.eml includes Giron, Gossett, Keiser, Baumbach and McLaughlin but not Carole Frank.
- 263.eml and 154.eml show the reports hold rebook actions such as "Rebook to AEP Energy Services, Inc." and "Rebook from ENA to ECC (Under the ISDA)".
- 154.eml forwards the 3/12/01 report a week late with "I don't know if you got any of these while I was out."

The estimate of 2 minutes a forward, about 21 times a month, is realistic, and it is close to the figure already saved.

**Research:** None needed, since more evidence would not change a duplicate verdict. The one thing that could make this new work is another desk lead's sent mail showing they also relay the report, such as Gossett, Keiser, Baumbach or McLaughlin. That would belong as an addition to item 3, not as a separate proposal.

content.text:
I saved the proposal, with a lower estimate: **220 minutes x 1.17 times a month = 4.29 hours, about $365 a month**. It is item 3 of 5 in `decisions.md`. Your draft claimed about $468.

**The idea and the evidence hold up.** Every quote I used is word for word in the mail. The other dated messages you listed do exist and cover the same work, from 27 Oct 2000 to 2 May 2001. Messages 192, 168 and 246 also confirm the Aquila Canada case: deals booked as ENA with a counterparty that has an ECC master swap.

**An earlier proposal for the same work was rejected** (`decisions.md`, item 21). Its rule only caught deals where ECC was the Enron party. That misses the deals that actually hold up invoicing: ENA deals with Aquila or Duke. It also ignored the EnronOnline program that already exists for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada. Your change fixes both problems. It extends that program to every counterparty with an ECC master and flags ENA deals with those names. So I treated it as a fixed version of that proposal, not a duplicate.

**What I changed:**
- **The estimate.** The check counts each round of requests as one time: 8 rounds over October 2000 to March 2001, so 1.17 a month. Several rounds belong to the same month, for example 27 Oct and 1 Nov, or 28 and 29 Mar. Your 360-minute total for a whole month already included a follow-up round, so applying it to every round would count that work twice. I rebuilt it per round:
  - Vallejo's search and list: about 60 minutes.
  - Forwarding: about 10 minutes.
  - About 12 people each searching their books for about 15 minutes. Many replies say "if applicable", so not everyone has deals to move.
  - Follow-ups: about 40 minutes.
  - Less about 30 minutes still needed to handle the nightly flags.

  That comes to about 260 minutes per round, which I cut to 220 so the extra rounds within a month are not overcounted.
- **The rate.** I set the stated rate to null. No message says how often the work happens, so the check worked it out from the dates of the rounds.
- **The wording.** Plain wording for managers. The "today" section now says why searching by hand misses deals: ENA deals with a Canadian counterparty don't show up as ECC deals (108.eml).

**One thing to keep in mind:** the mail doesn't show whether the Duke booking program was ever set up after Jan 2001. If it was, part of the rule is already in place, though the Aquila deals in March 2001 show the gap was still there.

The proposal file is `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-8\proposals\ecc-deals-houston-books.json`, and the record is in `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-8\decisions.md`.
