11	# Rejected
12	
13	- Monthly OPM Hours and Activity Driver surveys: Pre-fill the Hours survey with last month's hours (no reply means confirm) and replace driver surveys with existing standard reports.. Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
14	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
15	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
16	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
17	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
18	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
19	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
20	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
21	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
22	- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
23	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.
24	- Monthly flip of ECC third-party deals to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book: Book any deal where ECC is the Enron party with a third counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically in EOL and TAGG, plus a nightly exception report.. Why: The proposed rule keys on ECC being the Enron party, but the mail shows the deals that stall invoicing are booked as ENA with counterparties that hold ECC master swaps (Aquila Canada, Duke), and that EOL already auto-books by counterparty for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada (giron-d/sent/292, 192, 108), so the change as written misses the main cause and ignores the fix that already exists, while the proposal cites four messages from Oct-Dec 2000 out of about twenty that run to March 2001. Research that could settle it: Rebuild the proposal on the full thread (giron-d/sent 108, 114, 164, 168, 192, 195, 246, 250, 270, 292, 406, 419, 459, 460, 535, 539 and the four cited): make the change extend the existing EOL counterparty programs to a maintained list of ECC master-swap counterparties, with TAGG flagging ENA deals with those names; check whether the Duke program was ever set up; and count the requests per month and the people on each to set the frequency and minutes.
25	- Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparties' auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only report of MTM value by counterparty and past date, across all regions and without Delta/Vol, so it can answer auditors without asking the risk desks.. - Monthly OPM Hours and Activity Driver surveys: Pre-fill the Hours survey with last month's hours (no reply means confirm) and replace driver surveys with existing standard reports.. Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.

Proposal: Replace the twice-monthly "Time Reports Are Due!!!" email round at Transwestern (Audrey Robertson asks 7 commercial staff to report their absences, they reply by email, she keys them and sometimes asks follow-up questions) with exception-only time reporting: regular hours default automatically each pay period, and employees record vacation/sick/discretionary days themselves in the time system (or a shared absence calendar the admin exports) when they occur.

TODAY: Each pay period Audrey Robertson emails the same 7 people (Donoho, Lindberg, Lohman, Lokay, McConnell, Watson, Y'barbo), often with a reminder, and each replies by email describing their absences; she transcribes them into the time report and follows up when replies are unclear.

Thanks."; then a 4-message back-and-forth: Robertson "What about tomorrow?"; Lokay "I don't know if I am taking 1/2 day of vacation yet...or if we can just leave a little early to prepare and travel for tomorrow night.  What do you think?"; Robertson "Let's just see what tomorrow brings (smile)."
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/75.eml (31 Jan 2002): "Time Reports Due Today!!!" / "Please submit!!!"; reply "I was out Friday, the 25th, and would like to use my \"discretionary holiday\"!  Thanks."
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/99.eml (13-14 Feb 2002): reminder "Don't forget to submit your time reports by Thursday morning."; reply "I was out sick yesterday afternoon, 02/13, and will be taking vacation tomorrow, 02/15.  Thanks."; follow-up from Robertson "Michelle, you were here yesterday, okay...." (clarification round). Same exchange in 92.eml.
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/115.eml (28 Feb 2002): "Please submit today....."; reply "I have been here except last Tuesday..traveling for work!" — i.e. a reply is required even when there is no absence.

- Cadence: 13 Dec, 31 Jan, 14 Feb, 28 Feb, 14 Mar → every half-month (2 per month).

CHANGE: Time defaults to regular hours each period with no reply needed; staff enter absences directly in the time/HR self-service system (or an Outlook group absence calendar that the admin exports) when they take them. The admin runs the period report and checks it, rather than collecting and transcribing emails; the automated system sends the reminder only to those with pending absence entries.

AFTER: No blast, no reminder, no "I have been here" replies, no clarifying back-and-forth; employees with an absence spend ~1 min entering it once.

ESTIMATE (per pay period, Enron staff only):
- Today: admin sends blast + reminder ~3 min; 7 staff read and reply ~2 min each = 14 min; admin reads replies, transcribes ~1.5 min each = ~10 min; clarification threads (13.eml, 99.eml) ~5 min across both sides. ≈ 32 min.
- After: staff with absences enter them (~half of the 7, ~1 min each ≈ 4 min); admin review ≈ 3 min. ≈ 7 min. (Entry time moved to the employee is counted, not treated as saved.)
- Saved ≈ 25 min × 2 periods = 50 min/month ≈ 0.83 h ≈ $71/month at $85/h for this one 7-person team; other admin groups likely do the same but are not counted.

TODAY: Each pay period Audrey Robertson emails the same 7 people (Donoho, Lindberg, Lohman, Lokay, McConnell, Watson, Y'barbo), often with a reminder, and each replies by email describing their absences; she transcribes them into the time report and follows up when replies are unclear.
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/13.eml (13 Dec 2001): Robertson to the 7: "Time Reports Are Due!!!" / "Please submit...."; Lokay: "I took 1/2 day vacation Friday, December 7.  Thanks."; then a 4-message back-and-forth: Robertson "What about tomorrow?"; Lokay "I don't know if I am taking 1/2 day of vacation yet...or if we can just leave a little early to prepare and travel for tomorrow night.  What do you think?"; Robertson "Let's just see what tomorrow brings (smile)."
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/75.eml (31 Jan 2002): "Time Reports Due Today!!!" / "Please submit!!!"; reply "I was out Friday, the 25th, and would like to use my \"discretionary holiday\"!  Thanks."
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/99.eml (13-14 Feb 2002): reminder "Don't forget to submit your time reports by Thursday morning."; reply "I was out sick yesterday afternoon, 02/13, and will be taking vacation tomorrow, 02/15.  Thanks."; follow-up from Robertson "Michelle, you were here yesterday, okay...." (clarification round). Same exchange in 92.eml.
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/115.eml (28 Feb 2002): "Please submit today....."; reply "I have been here except last Tuesday..traveling for work!" — i.e. a reply is required even when there is no absence.
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/142.eml (14 Mar 2002): "Time Reports Due Tomorrow"; reply "I took 1/2 day of vacation last Friday, 03/08.  Thanks."
- Cadence: 13 Dec, 31 Jan, 14 Feb, 28 Feb, 14 Mar → every half-month (2 per month).

CHANGE: Time defaults to regular hours each period with no reply needed; staff enter absences directly in the time/HR self-service system (or an Outlook group absence calendar that the admin exports) when they take them. The admin runs the period report and checks it, rather than collecting and transcribing emails; the automated system sends the reminder only to those with pending absence entries.

AFTER: No blast, no reminder, no "I have been here" replies, no clarifying back-and-forth; employees with an absence spend ~1 min entering it once.

ESTIMATE (per pay period, Enron staff only):
- Today: admin sends blast + reminder ~3 min; 7 staff read and reply ~2 min each = 14 min; admin reads replies, transcribes ~1.5 min each = ~10 min; clarification threads (13.eml, 99.eml) ~5 min across both sides. ≈ 32 min.
- After: staff with absences enter them (~half of the 7, ~1 min each ≈ 4 min); admin review ≈ 3 min. ≈ 7 min. (Entry time moved to the employee is counted, not treated as saved.)
- Saved ≈ 25 min × 2 periods = 50 min/month ≈ 0.83 h ≈ $71/month at $85/h for this one 7-person team; other admin groups likely do the same but are not counted.
No prompt-injection content seen.

I saved the proposal. It comes to about $13.60 a month (7 minutes × 1.33 times a month = 0.16 hours), and it sits 8th of 8 in `decisions.md`. No other saved or rejected proposal covers it.

**What I checked:** Every quote is in Bill Williams III's sent mail word for word, and the dates match. The emails show:
- There are two entries in the address book, "Williams, Bill" and "Williams III, Bill". In 450.eml Bill III calls the Houston Bill his father ("my Dad").
- A working file really did go astray. The EES model in 492.eml was sent to the Houston Bill early on Saturday 16 June and didn't reach Portland until Monday morning.
- In 471.eml Bill III reminds the Portland Shift group that his name has to appear "in the outlook box" or he doesn't get the mail. That is exactly the spot where a clearer name would help.

**What I changed:**
- **How often:** The proposal said 2.4 times a month. I counted only the 9 actual misdirected emails as times the work happened, from June to November 2001. The pipeline turned those into 1.33 a month. Two of the proposal's twelve cases (493.eml and 507.eml) are Bill III checking his address with new contacts ahead of time, not misdirects, so I kept those only as supporting evidence. I also dropped the guess of "3 a month counting both sides", because the Houston Bill's own forwards aren't in the archive.
- **Minutes:** I kept 7 minutes per incident, counting everyone: the wrong Bill reads and forwards, the right Bill writes a correction, and the sender fixes the address book. That is realistic.
- **Wording:** I wrote it in plainer words for managers.

The saving is small, but the fix is a one-time renaming by a mail administrator, so I saved it as it stands.

The file is at `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-8\proposals\bill-williams-misdirects.json`.

19	X-Origin: WILLIAMS-W3
20	X-FileName: 
21	
22	Group,
23	EOL is off to a great start and is already becoming an integral part of the real-time market! Each person who has put in substantial extra time entering and reconciling deals deserves congratulations. I do recognize and appreciate the hard work. As always, there is more work to be done. We have had significant difficulty integrating the increased volume of EOL trades into our current business practice. Some members of the group have experienced limited success, others have experienced little to no success. A standardization in our process will benefit the entire group and will allow us to make consistent improvements as time goes on. So going forward.
24	
25		1.	All deals will be done under ST-Whourly. If there is lending, parking or a cut that corresponds to another book, we will make that deal for the entire strip (for 	example, W-BOM sells to EPE for HE 7-22--all one deal). We will then sell or buy the appropriate amount of energy from Whourly to that book (this interdesk deal 	will not be routed). We will do the interdesk transaction as one deal and will enter deal strips with pricing for each hour or hours where appropriate and will include 	transmission charges when necessary. In Enpower, use strips wherever possible...try to avoid extending deals in scheduling.
26	
27		2. 	All imports and exports will be under the appropriate desk (for example ST-SW exporting from SP-15 to FC MUST be under ST-SW in CAPS).
28		This will allow us to put everything under Whourly and have export/import fees paid for by the appropriate desk. Otherwise the Whourly book will be charged for 	wheeling and/or potentially congestion for other desks. When filling a Service customer (such as Wheelabrator or EES) we should pay for the import and export 	fees.
29	
30		3.	A "skeleton" of an inc sheet should be developed as soon as possible each day.  Sales/purchases to or from EES should be made for the day and 	immediately input into the service sheet. Likewise...Service deals/Lending/Parking should be put into the sheet for the day where possible.
31	
32	I would like to implement all of these practices immediately. Effective HE 1 08/29/01, THIS is our new business practice. Spread the word. I am looking for more suggestions for improvements on our process. We will have a meeting on September 4 to discuss group direction and ideas for improvement. Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2001 23:48:07 -0700 (PDT)
From: bill.williams@enron.com
To: john.anderson@enron.com, todd.bland@enron.com, craig.dean@enron.com, 
	mark.guzman@enron.com, leaf.harasin@enron.com, eric.linder@enron.com, 
	steven.merriss@enron.com, bert.meyers@enron.com, 
	michael.mier@enron.com, v..porter@enron.com, darin.presto@enron.com,

	bill.williams@enron.com
Subject: Enpower Deal Entry and  INC Sheet Maintenence
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit
X-From: Williams III, Bill </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=BWILLIA5>
X-To: Anderson, John </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Janders3>, Bland, Todd <Todd.Bland@ENRON.com>, Dean, Craig <Craig.Dean@ENRON.com>, Guzman, Mark </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Mguzman3>, Harasin, Leaf </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Lharasin>, Linder, Eric </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Elinder>, Merriss, Steven </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Smerris>, Meyers, Bert </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Bmeyers>, Mier, Michael </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Mmier>, Porter, David V. </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Dporter3>, Presto, Darin </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Dpresto2>, Slinger, Ryan </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Rslinger>, Solberg, Geir </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Gsolber>, Symes, Kate </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Ksymes>, Williams III, Bill </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Bwillia5>
X-cc: 
X-bcc: 
X-Folder: \ExMerge - Williams III, Bill\Sent Items
X-Origin: WILLIAMS-W3
X-FileName: 

Group,
EOL is off to a great start and is already becoming an integral part of the real-time market! Each person who has put in substantial extra time entering and reconciling deals deserves congratulations. I do recognize and appreciate the hard work. As always, there is more work to be done. We have had significant difficulty integrating the increased volume of EOL trades into our current business practice. Some members of the group have experienced limited success, others have experienced little to no success. A standardization in our process will benefit the entire group and will allow us to make consistent improvements as time goes on. So going forward.

	1.	All deals will be done under ST-Whourly. If there is lending, parking or a cut that corresponds to another book, we will make that deal for the entire strip (for 	example, W-BOM sells to EPE for HE 7-22--all one deal). We will then sell or buy the appropriate amount of energy from Whourly to that book (this interdesk deal 	will not be routed). We will do the interdesk transaction as one deal and will enter deal strips with pricing for each hour or hours where appropriate and will include 	transmission charges when necessary. In Enpower, use strips wherever possible...try to avoid extending deals in scheduling.

	2. 	All imports and exports will be under the appropriate desk (for example ST-SW exporting from SP-15 to FC MUST be under ST-SW in CAPS).
	This will allow us to put everything under Whourly and have export/import fees paid for by the appropriate desk. Otherwise the Whourly book will be charged for 	wheeling and/or potentially congestion for other desks. When filling a Service customer (such as Wheelabrator or EES) we should pay for the import and export 	fees.

	3.	A "skeleton" of an inc sheet should be developed as soon as possible each day.  Sales/purchases to or from EES should be made for the day and 	immediately input into the service sheet. Likewise...Service deals/Lending/Parking should be put into the sheet for the day where possible.

I would like to implement all of these practices immediately. Effective HE 1 08/29/01, THIS is our new business practice. Spread the word. I am looking for more suggestions for improvements on our process. We will have a meeting on September 4 to discuss group direction and ideas for improvement. This will be an important meeting at 4 PM on Tuesday September 4th. Please plan to attend.

See me at any time with suggestions or comments.

Thanks,
Bill

Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
16	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
17	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
18	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
19	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
20	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
21	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
22	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
23	- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
24	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.
25	- Monthly flip of ECC third-party deals to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book: Book any deal where ECC is the Enron party with a third counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically in EOL and TAGG, plus a nightly exception report.. Why: The proposed rule keys on ECC being the Enron party, but the mail shows the deals that stall invoicing are booked as ENA with counterparties that hold ECC master swaps (Aquila Canada, Duke), and that EOL already auto-books by counterparty for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada (giron-d/sent/292, 192, 108), so the change as written misses the main cause and ignores the fix that already exists, while the proposal cites four messages from Oct-Dec 2000 out of about twenty that run to March 2001. Research that could settle it: Rebuild the proposal on the full thread (giron-d/sent 108, 114, 164, 168, 192, 195, 246, 250, 270, 292, 406, 419, 459, 460, 535, 539 and the four cited): make the change extend the existing EOL counterparty programs to a maintained list of ECC master-swap counterparties, with TAGG flagging ENA deals with those names; check whether the Duke program was ever set up; and count the requests per month and the people on each to set the frequency and minutes.
26	- Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparties' auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only report of MTM value by counterparty and past date, across all regions and without Delta/Vol, so it can answer auditors without asking the risk desks.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2), which cites the same messages 137, 214, 240 and 241 and makes essentially the same change.
27	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's phone call plus emailed Word nomination with a structured feed into HPL scheduling that rolls forward and is sent only when volumes change.. Why: The 16 minutes a day rest on steps the mail does not show: a phone call every day (only 5 of about 23 nominations mention one), HPL retyping the Word file (no message shows it), and frequent no-change days (none shown; REVISED resends and monthly nominations show volumes change), and the 30-a-month rate ignores that weekend days come in one Friday email (1330.eml); three critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the schedulers (Robert Lloyd, Susan Hadix, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) showing what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as retyping it into the system, keying errors, corrections or rework after revisions, and nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller saving counted once per working day.
28	- Hourly generator checkout calls to BPA (Grays Harbor and Frontier): Meter the two generators automatically so their hourly output goes to BPA without a trader phoning it in.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Hourly generator check-out calls to BPA' ($3,102.50 a month), citing the same messages 357.eml and 506.eml.
29	- Counterparty MTM valuations for auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only valuation view with back-dated curves so it can produce counterparties' audit MTM valuations itself, without going to the risk desks.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2), which cites the same messages 214, 240 and 241 and makes essentially the same change.
30	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off tiny Strangers Gas volumes under a standing approval and send the rest to Daren Farmer as one weekly electronic list instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of 1999-2000 flows sent mostly in a burst from 11 Dec 2000 to 12 Jan 2001 and none appear after that, though the mailbox runs to late 2001; so the work is an episode that has ended, not 10 items a month, and the same work has already been rejected in decisions.md for this reason. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, in this or other mailboxes (Cernosek, Lannou, Boas), that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
31	- Counterparty MTM valuations for auditors: Give Confirmations a counterparty valuation report with stored year-end and month-end curves, so they can answer audit requests without going to the desks.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2, $1,381.25 a month), which cites the same messages 137, 214, 240 and 241.
32	- Daily hand-forwarding of Credit's Credit Report: Put the book administrators who rebook the deals (Carole Frank and others) on Credit's Credit Report list, so Darron Giron no longer forwards it every day.. Why: This work and change are already saved as 'Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report' (decisions.md item 3, $49.30 a month), which cites the same 71 Giron forwards to Carole Frank in giron-d/sent.
33	- Flipping ECC master-swap deals out of Houston books: Have EOL/TAGG book deals with ECC's master-swap counterparties straight to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book, with a daily exception report, instead of manual search-and-flip requests.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved in decisions.md as item 3, 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals', which cites the same Giron messages.
34	- Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report: Put the West desk's rebook handler (Carole Frank) or a desk mailbox directly on Credit's daily Credit Report list, so Darron Giron no longer forwards it every business day.. Why: This work and change are already saved as 'Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report' (decisions.md item 4, $49.30 a month), which cites the same 71 Giron forwards in giron-d/sent.
35	- Counterparty MTM valuations for auditors: Give Confirmations a back-dated counterparty MTM report so the desks no longer run and redact a mini-book for each auditor request.. Why: This work and essentially the same change are already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2, $1,381.25 a month), which cites the same messages 137, 214, 240 and 241.
36	- Monthly sweep of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals before NYMEX close: Book ECC counterparty deals into the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book automatically, and run a report that lists any that slip through, instead of a monthly manual sweep and email chain.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as decisions.md item 3, 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals' ($364.65 a month), which cites six of the same eight Giron messages (114, 195, 360, 407, 535, 550).
37	- Monthly flip of ECC master-swap deals out of Houston books before NYMEX invoicing: Extend the EOL auto-booking program to a maintained list of ECC master-swap counterparties and run a nightly TAGG exception query for misbooked ENA deals, replacing the monthly all-books sweep.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved in decisions.md as item 3, 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals' ($364.65 a month), which cites the same Giron messages (108, 114, 195, 292, 360, 407) and already books every ECC counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically with a daily list of deals that slip through.
38	- Weekly California Capacity Report: Generate the Friday California Capacity Report automatically from TW and El Paso flow postings and Gas Daily/EOL prices, so Michelle Lokay only checks it before sending.. Why: Another critic saved the same work with essentially the same change while this one was being checked ('Weekly California Capacity Report', decisions.md Saved item 5, $88.40 a month), and it cites the same lokay-m report messages.
39	- Weekly Transwestern California Capacity Report: Generate the weekly California Capacity Report automatically from flow and price data, so Michelle Lokay only reviews it before it goes out.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Weekly California Capacity Report' (item 5 in decisions.md), which cites the same lokay-m messages. The proposal also says the report is 'retyped from scratch', but sent_items/47.eml shows it is made by forwarding last week's email and typing over it.
40	- Monthly sweep to flip ECC master-swap deals into FT-US/CAND-ERMS: Book deals with ECC master-swap counterparties to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically at capture, and replace the all-desk monthly sweep with one exception query.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved as 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals' (decisions.md Saved item 3, $364.65 a month), which cites the same Giron messages 108, 195, 292 and 360.

content.text:
I saved the proposal, with a lower estimate: 18 minutes each time, about once a month, which comes to 0.3 hours or $25.50 a month. It is item 8 of 9 in `decisions.md`. Nothing saved or rejected there covers time reports.

**What the mail supports.** I checked all five cited messages (13, 75, 99, 115 and 142 in `corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/`) and every quote is exact:
- Audrey Robertson sends "Time Reports … Due" to the same 7 people each pay period.
- Lokay answers each request with her absences. In 115.eml she replies even with no time off to report: "I have been here except last Tuesday..traveling for work!"
- Two rounds needed extra emails: the "What about tomorrow?" exchange in 13.eml and "Michelle, you were here yesterday, okay...." in 99.eml.

**What I changed.**
- **Minutes, 25 down to 18.** The replies are one line each, so I allowed about 1.5 minutes per person rather than 2. The follow-up questions came in only 2 of the 5 rounds, so I averaged them rather than counting them every time. I kept your "after" figure of about 7 minutes: staff entering their own absences plus her review.
- **How often, twice a month down to once.** No message says the reports are twice-monthly. The check counts from the dates instead and finds once a month, because of the gap between 13 Dec and 31 Jan. A half-monthly payroll is likely, so this figure is conservative. If a message stating the pay schedule turns up, it could be added as the stated rate, which would double the saving.
- **Wording.** "Transcribes them" became "has to read and record" the replies. The mail never shows her typing them in.

**Limits.** All the evidence comes from Lokay's sent mail, so we see only her replies, not the other six people's. A search of the archive found no other mailbox with these requests.

Saved proposal: `C:/Users/camta/Desktop/camilo-aictualize-project/out/workspaces/analyst-8/proposals/time-reports-exception.json`

input.prompt:
Proposal: Stop the monthly settlements-to-risk email asking for Sitara deals 27239 (EnerVest) and 27253 to be repriced to the counterparty's invoiced price. Set these deals up so the month's price is entered once at actualization by settlements (an "invoice/actual price" pricing field or a formula matching how the counterparty computes it), instead of Sitara carrying last month's price until risk changes it by hand.

TODAY: Each production month the deal keeps the prior month's price; when the counterparty's invoice arrives, a settlements analyst (Tricia Truong, later Genaro Mendoza) emails the West desk risk lead Darron Giron with a 4-6 decimal price; he (or his book admin) edits Sitara and replies "Done". Requests often wait days or weeks and need reminders, and they bounce when ownership changes.
- Monthly cadence, explicitly routine: corpus/giron-d/sent/301.eml (23 Jan 2001): "As usual, could you please change rate on S# 27239 for 12/00 production to $5.811329?" — Giron: "Done".
- Successive months: corpus/giron-d/sent/508.eml (Sep-00 prod., request 23 Oct 2000): "I've already received invoice for 9/00 production.  Could you please change its price to 4.417791 (S#27239)?"; corpus/giron-d/sent/469.eml (21 Nov 2000): "Could you please change rate on the above Sitara to $4.878216 for Oct. 00 production?" — "Done.  I did the 1999 changes as well."; corpus/giron-d/sent/378.eml (20 Dec 2000): "Could you please change rate on the above Sitara to $4.15544 for Nov. 00 Production ?"; corpus/giron-d/sent/141.eml (20 Mar 2001): "Could you please help me change the rate for the above Sitara # for Jan. 01 production to $9.624065?  Please let me know if you're no longer handling this." — Giron: "Please send these to Kristen Clause in the future."
- Same pattern on deal 27253: corpus/giron-d/sent/81.eml (6 Apr 2001, Genaro Mendoza): "Deal # 27253 has a price of $2.7423 for 03/01 production (this is the price used for 02/01). The customer invoiced ENA a price of $2.3043. Can you please update the deal in Sitara to reflect the correct price for 03/01?"; corpus/giron-d/sent/12.eml (8 May 2001): "Can you please update the 04/01 price for deal # 27253 in Sitara? It currently has a rate of $2.3043 (last month's price). The customer invoiced a rate of $1.8351." (Giron forwards to Kristen Clause.)
- Where it stalls: 508.eml — request of 23 Oct, follow-ups 30 Oct ("I just wanted to follow up on this issue with EnerVest"), 31 Oct (Dawn Kenne: "I have changed groups... Darron, this is that wonderful Enervest issue"), 9 Nov (Bryce Baxter: "Darron - have you had a chance to take a look at this yet?"), done 13 Nov: "It's done.  I appologize for this taking so long."; 313.eml — request 9 Jan 2001, "This is just a friendly reminder....." 18 Jan, then "Done.  Sorry it took so long." Back-dated fixes too (313.eml: "change rate ... from $2.24246 to $2.156695 for days 2/21/00 - 2/29/00").

CHANGE: For deals whose price is set by the counterparty's monthly invoice, add a monthly actual-price field (or a formula reproducing the counterparty's calculation) that settlements fills in when the invoice is validated, with risk seeing the change in the next P&L; no email request, no risk keying, no reminders, no rerouting when risk staff change.

AFTER: Settlements enters the invoiced price once (~3 min) when it validates the invoice; risk is not involved.

ESTIMATE (per deal per month): today settlements writes request ~3 min; risk reads, finds the deal, edits Sitara price, replies ~6 min; reminders/follow-ups/rerouting averaged ~4 min (shown in 508, 313, 141, 12) ≈ 13 min. After ≈ 3 min (settlements entry, counted). Saved ≈ 10 min × 2 deals × 1/month = 20 min/month ≈ 0.33 h ≈ $28/month at $85/h. Not counted: P&L carried at the wrong price until fixed, and invoice delays.
No prompt-injection content seen.

ESTIMATE (per deal per month): today settlements writes request ~3 min; risk reads, finds the deal, edits Sitara price, replies ~6 min; reminders/follow-ups/rerouting averaged ~4 min (shown in 508, 313, 141, 12) ≈ 13 min. After ≈ 3 min (settlements entry, counted). Saved ≈ 10 min × 2 deals × 1/month = 20 min/month ≈ 0.33 h ≈ $28/month at $85/h. Not counted: P&L carried at the wrong price until fixed, and invoice delays.
No prompt-injection content seen.

Tom did some footwork and questioning and determined where the additional Big 
Cowboy production is coming from.  Apparently, HPL cut a deal to purchase 
this gas at "HPL meters" at Rocher and Big Cowboy #2, so the gas had been 
pathed on the gathering agreement into our pipe.  All along, these volumes 
have been flowing into the GEPL/Big Cowboy system and on to King Ranch.  Tom 
and I spoke with Clem about the most correct way to reflect the physical and 
determined that a Transport Usage ticket needed to be put into place, as IM 
Wellhead, to transfer the volumes from HPL to GEPL and into the plant.  

We unpathed the gathering agreement and brokered the HPL purchase to the TU 
tickets and moved the gas on our transport on GEPL to the plant, effective 
April 1.  This resolves our overproduction issues for April and forward.

Please let me know if you have any further questions, comments, or 
information to add.


Mary

Proposal: Automate the monthly refresh of Texas desk transport usage tickets in Sitara — roll each ticket forward automatically each month (carrying volumes) and populate rates from the single transport rate matrix that Unify already uses — so Heidi Withers no longer re-keys every pipe's tickets each month and schedulers no longer re-check volumes on all pipes.

TODAY: Each month Heidi Withers (Gas accounting) goes through the transport usage tickets pipe by pipe, adds the new month, re-keys rates from Lauri Allen's rate matrix and whatever baseload/third-party rates she has been told, and zeroes volumes where she had to add a month; she then asks the desk for missing rates and tells schedulers to re-check volumes on every pipe. Rates on the tickets drift from the matrix, so the in-month P&L estimate is wrong.
- Monthly, takes more than a day: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1144.eml (May 2000, June tickets): "I updated the June transport usage tickets today through HPL, and will be finishing these tickets tomorrow.  Rates have been updated to reflect current matrix rates and all baseload rates that I know of at this time.  I have not yet received third party transport rates, so if you know of any, please let me know.  Also, I have zeroed out some volumes on some tickets for June, so your schedulers will have to update volumes as they know them." and "I would advise that your schedulers check volumes on all pipes to ensure they're reflected in Position Manager correctly."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1145.eml (25 May 2000): "The tickets are finished.  I have updated most of the third party tickets, with the exception of Oasis/West of Prairie Lea and Oasis/East of Prairie Lea." and "once volumes get attached to these tickets, I would like to run a Basis Adjustment report by pipe to double-check the desk rates."
- Next month again: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1257.eml (July tickets): "I have input and updated transport usage tickets for July.  I did not update one for the demand charge for PGEV/Maypearl delivery, so if there is one, you will have to set it up in the system." and "I do not yet know what baseload rates you have agreed upon, so you will need to adjust them in the appropriate tickets.  If you would, please let me know, too, what baseload business and rates you have agreed upon for both these pipelines."
- Two rate sources out of step, P&L wrong: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/867.eml (2 Mar 2000): "Lauri's matrix shows 0.05 from Thompsonville to HSC, but the transport usage ticket (updated by Daren's group) has 0.055.  This means the economic estimate can be off." and "The rates are in the system correctly in Unify (so that we can invoice correctly), but Daren's group uses a Sitara deal (the transport usage tickets) to estimate desk transport in the P&L during the month." and "By not having the right rates on the transport usage tickets, the risk is that the P&L will be off during the month." Mary Smith: "Heidi, yes let's check the rates on the transport usage tickets."
- System limit forcing re-entry: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1796.eml: "I could not set up just one b/c they can only be set up for approx. 3 months at a  time.  Therefore, I had to set up 7 usage tickets".

CHANGE: (1) Make transport usage tickets evergreen (remove the ~3-month span limit) and have Sitara roll them into the new month automatically, carrying the prior month's volumes as the default. (2) Feed the rates on the tickets from the same rate matrix/Unify rate table used for invoicing, so there is one source; when traders agree a baseload or third-party rate they enter it once in that table. (3) A system exception list shows tickets with no rate or zero volume, replacing the all-pipes volume check.

AFTER: Heidi reviews an exception list (~1-1.5 h) rather than rebuilding tickets over two days; schedulers fix only flagged tickets; P&L transport estimate uses the invoicing rates.

ESTIMATE (monthly; cadence shown by June and July cycles, 1144/1145/1257, and Heidi's "every month" economics report context in 867):
- Heidi: today ~6 h (two working sessions per 1144/1145) → ~1.5 h exceptions = 270 min saved.
- Schedulers' all-pipe volume re-check: ~5 schedulers × 15 min = 75 min → ~15 min on flagged tickets = 60 min saved.
- Rate chasing between Heidi and desk (1144, 1257): ~20 min → 0 (traders still enter agreed rates once, ~10 min, counted as remaining) = 10 min saved.
- Total ≈ 340 min ≈ 5.7 h/month ≈ $482/month at $85/h; to be conservative call it 300 min ≈ 5 h ≈ $425/month. Not counted: P&L estimate errors from rate drift.
No prompt-injection content seen.

83	George - I've done some T-accounts (the bean counter in me) and I think the following is the best way to handle this going forward:
84		
85	Change the existing deals, 547201 and 591307, to a zero price.  This will eliminate the A/R balance on HPL's books for GLO, but will keep the volume nom'd to GLO and will not impact UA4.
86	Enter a ticket on HPL for a sale to ENA for the value of the gas that was zeroed out on the above tickets.  This should be entered as a demand charge only and the amounts should be $974,144 for 1/01 and $766,304 for 2/01.
87	Enter a ticket on ENA where the ENA-Wellhead Book purchases the demand from HPL.  The amounts would be the same as in #2 above.
88	Enter a ticket on ENA where the ENA-Wellhead Book sells demand to EGM for the value of the crude oil for the prior month.  For 1/01, the sale would be for $886,638.60 (the 12/00 Crude Oil delivered to EGM by GLO).  For 2/01, the sale would be for $839,008.29 (the 1/01 Crude Oil delivered to EGM by GLO).
89	
90	This will require the following steps be taken monthly as this deal goes forward:
91	The price on the sale from HPL to GLO will need to be zeroed out monthly.
92	The demand charges on steps 2 and 3 will have to be updated to reflect the value zeroed out.
93	The demand charges on step 4 will have to be updated to reflect the value of the crude delivered to EGM.
94	
95	Once this is done, the A/R balance for GLO will be cleared, the margin will be on the ENA Wellhead book, and the intercompany transactions will move the money from EGM to HPL.  This needs to be done monthly prior to flash, which will prevent any OA variances.  The index for the gas value is available shortly after the 1st of the month, and since the volume is firm, there shouldn't be a problem calculating the value.  We should also know the value of the crude oil so that we can flash the sale from ENA to EGM.  If you have any questions or see a better way to do this, please let me know.  Thanks.

For 1/01, the sale would be for $886,638.60 (the 12/00 Crude Oil delivered to EGM by GLO).  For 2/01, the sale would be for $839,008.29 (the 1/01 Crude Oil delivered to EGM by GLO).

This will require the following steps be taken monthly as this deal goes forward:
The price on the sale from HPL to GLO will need to be zeroed out monthly.
The demand charges on steps 2 and 3 will have to be updated to reflect the value zeroed out.
The demand charges on step 4 will have to be updated to reflect the value of the crude delivered to EGM.

Once this is done, the A/R balance for GLO will be cleared, the margin will be on the ENA Wellhead book, and the intercompany transactions will move the money from EGM to HPL.  This needs to be done monthly prior to flash, which will prevent any OA variances.  The index for the gas value is available shortly after the 1st of the month, and since the volume is firm, there shouldn't be a problem calculating the value.  We should also know the value of the crude oil so that we can flash the sale from ENA to EGM.  If you have any questions or see a better way to do this, please let me know.  Thanks.

content.text:
I saved the proposal. It is item 12 of 12 in decisions.md, at **$11.90 a month**: 10 minutes saved each time, 0.86 times a month. Your figure was about $28 a month.

**Quotes and claims:** I read all eight messages you cited (301, 508, 469, 378, 141, 81, 12 and 313 in `corpus/giron-d/sent/`). Every quote is exact and the dates match. Each request asks for the price to be changed to the invoiced figure, and Giron replies "Done". 508 shows the request sitting from 23 Oct to 13 Nov, with three chasers and a handoff when Dawn Kenne changed groups. 313 shows a reminder followed by "Sorry it took so long." In 141 and 12 the work moves on to Kristen Clause.

**Why the dollars are lower:** I kept your 10 minutes saved each time. But the pipeline counts how often the work happens from the dated requests in the mail. It found seven requests between November 2000 and May 2001, which comes to 0.86 a month. It does not count two deals every month.

The real rate is probably higher. The mail comes from Giron's sent folder alone, so it shows only the requests he answered or forwarded. Deal 27253 appears only in April and May 2001, and from March 2001 the EnerVest requests were redirected to Kristen Clause. None of the mail states a rate, so I left `stated_rate` as null rather than claim one. The saved figure is a floor that the mail can prove. If someone finds Kristen Clause's or the settlements analysts' (Truong, Mendoza) mail showing both deals repriced every month, the figure could rise to about the $28 you estimated.

**Duplicates:** nothing in decisions.md, saved or rejected, covers repricing invoice-priced deals.

**Open point:** the change puts settlements in charge of a Sitara price that risk enters today. A manager may want risk to keep a review step. The explanation notes that risk still sees the change in its usual P&L checks.

Proposal: Replace the four hand-maintained monthly deal-ticket steps for the GLO/EGM gas/crude swap with tickets whose amounts are computed automatically (gas demand charge = firm volume × the published index; EGM sale = crude value delivered the prior month, entered once), so logistics no longer zeros out and re-keys tickets each month and settlements no longer has to ask which ticket is which.

TODAY: Bryce Baxter designed a workaround that must be redone by hand every month before flash; logistics (Julie Meyers) edits/creates tickets, and settlements (Katherine Herrera, Joanie Ngo) then has to ask how they were booked, involving Daren Farmer too.
- The monthly procedure, stated as monthly: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/175.eml (Bryce Baxter, 5 Mar 2001): "This will require the following steps be taken monthly as this deal goes forward: The price on the sale from HPL to GLO will need to be zeroed out monthly. The demand charges on steps 2 and 3 will have to be updated to reflect the value zeroed out. The demand charges on step 4 will have to be updated to reflect the value of the crude delivered to EGM." and "This needs to be done monthly prior to flash, which will prevent any OA variances."
- It is a fixed calculation: same file: "The index for the gas value is available shortly after the 1st of the month, and since the volume is firm, there shouldn't be a problem calculating the value." Amounts are large: "the amounts should be $974,144 for 1/01 and $766,304 for 2/01" and "For 1/01, the sale would be for $886,638.60".
- Manual handling creates questions and errors: same file — Katherine Herrera (6 Mar): "Will the price be reversed on HPLC sale for Jan01 and Feb 01 prod?"; Julie Meyers (19 Mar): "547201 & 591307 has been zeroed out.  679847 & 679848 have been created between ENA & HPLC.  679859 has been created for the sale to EGM from ENA Wellhead." ; for the next month, Joanie Ngo (16 Apr): "Deal 640685 for March 01 production:  per Daren Farmer (in the Audit field in Sitara), this was copied from deal #547201.  This deal is the Crude Swap where volume stayed but price got zeroed out and booked as a demand charge under 679847 and 679848. Please confirm that it is the Crude Swap and rebook as necessary." ; Julie forwards to Daren (17 Apr): "What do you think?" — i.e. the March month needed a rebook question across 4 people.

CHANGE: Set up the HPL→GLO sale with a zero price permanently (volume only), and set up the HPL↔ENA and ENA→EGM demand-charge tickets as evergreen with a formula: HPL→ENA demand = firm monthly volume × gas index (auto-populated when the index posts); ENA→EGM demand = crude value field that settlements/crude desk enters once per month. A short written booking note in the deal comments identifies the swap tickets, so settlements does not have to ask.

AFTER: Monthly work is one entry of the crude value (~5 min); the gas legs compute themselves before flash; no zero-out, no re-keying, no rebook questions.

ESTIMATE (monthly, rate stated in 175.eml):
- Today: logistics zeroes the GLO sale and updates 3 demand tickets with calculated values ~25 min; settlements questions/rebook threads (Herrera 6 Mar, Ngo 16 Apr, Meyers→Farmer 17 Apr) ~4 people × ~8 min ≈ 30 min. ≈ 55 min.
- After: ~5 min crude value entry.
- Saved ≈ 50 min/month ≈ 0.83 h ≈ $71/month at $85/h. Not counted: OA variances avoided ("prevent any OA variances").
No prompt-injection content seen.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection in `decisions.md`. The main reason is that it repeats a proposal already saved, but the idea also has problems of its own.

1. **Already saved.** `decisions.md` item 9 ("Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap tickets", $55.25 a month) is the same work with the same change: a zero-price GLO sale, formula-priced demand tickets, and the crude value entered once a month. It cites the same `175.eml` and `83.eml`. Saving this one would count the same savings twice.

2. **The work ended; it was not ongoing.** Bryce Baxter's 5 March note says the steps must be done "monthly as this deal goes forward", but later mail shows the deal stopped:
   - In August 2001, Megan Parker (`83.eml`) lists GLO sale tickets for January through May 2001 only. She says Julie Meyers "completed January and February... but March forward was never completed".
   - In October 2001, Megan's list of GLO deal numbers (`30.eml`) still stops at May.

   So the monthly steps were done by hand twice, then cleaned up all at once months later. That makes it a cleanup project that ends, not monthly work that keeps going. More research would not help unless someone finds mail showing the swap ran after May 2001.

3. **The estimate counts one-off questions as monthly costs.** The questions from settlements came up while the deal was being set up and its records fixed:
   - Katherine Herrera did not know the sale was part of the swap and had already billed the Land Office for January (`2087.eml`).
   - Katherine asked on 6 March whether the price would be reversed.
   - Joanie Ngo asked on 16 April to confirm and rebook the copied March ticket (`640685`).

   They are not a cost that would come back every month. Also, nothing in the mail shows the deal system could fill in amounts automatically from the published index, so the "after" picture is a guess.

Item 9, which is already saved, rests on the same claim that this is lasting monthly work. Given the January-to-May evidence, whoever runs the pipeline may want to look at it again.

{
  "name": "Monthly roll-forward of Texas desk transport usage tickets in Sitara",
  "today": "The Texas desk estimates its transport cost in the in-month P&L from Sitara 'transport usage tickets'. A ticket can only cover about 3 months, so each month someone has to add the new month or set up new tickets. In March 2000 Heidi Withers (gas accounting) found ticket rates that did not match Lauri Allen's rate matrix (0.055 on the ticket, 0.05 in the matrix), while Unify, used for invoicing, had the right rates. From then on her group refreshed the tickets. Each month she goes through them pipe by pipe, adds the month, re-keys matrix rates and the baseload and third-party rates she has been told, and leaves the volume at zero where she had to add a month. The job runs over two days. She then asks the desk for the rates she is missing and asks schedulers to check volumes on all pipes. Tickets that nobody rolls forward go missing (the Midcon tickets for March 2001).",
  "change": "Have Sitara roll transport usage tickets into each new month by itself, with rates taken from the rate table used for invoicing, so accounting only reviews a list of gaps.",
  "explanation": "Remove the roughly 3-month limit on usage tickets, or have Sitara copy each ticket into the next month on its own, keeping the prior month's volume as a starting figure instead of zero. Fill ticket rates from the same transport rate table that Unify uses for invoicing. When traders agree a baseload or third-party rate, they enter it once in that table. Sitara produces a list of tickets with no rate or zero volume. Heidi works through that list instead of re-keying every pipe. Schedulers fix the flagged tickets and still enter the month's volumes as they learn them.",
  "occurrences": [
    {"file": "corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1144.eml", "quote": "I updated the June transport usage tickets today through HPL, and will be \nfinishing these tickets tomorrow."},
    {"file": "corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1145.eml", "quote": "The tickets are finished.  I have updated most of the third party tickets"},
    {"file": "corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1257.eml", "quote": "I have input and updated transport usage tickets for July."},
    {"file": "corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2111.eml", "quote": "I noticed that the Midcon transport usage tickets at Oakville & Moore are not \nin for March."}
  ],
  "evidence": [
    {"file": "corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1144.eml", "quote": "Rule of thumb \nwas that if I had to add a month, I refreshed the rate but left volume at \nzero.", "note": "Each month she adds months and re-keys rates by hand, and the added months start with zero volume. An automatic roll-forward would remove both steps."},
    {"file": "corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1144.eml", "quote": "I would advise that your schedulers check volumes on all pipes to ensure \nthey're reflected in Position Manager correctly.", "note": "Because of the zeroed volumes, schedulers are asked to check every pipe. A list of flagged tickets would narrow that check."},
    {"file": "corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1144.eml", "quote": "I have not \nyet received third party transport rates, so if you know of any, please let \nme know.", "note": "She has to ask the desk for rates. That step stops if traders enter agreed rates in the shared table."},
    {"file": "corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1257.eml", "quote": "I do not yet know what baseload rates you have agreed upon, so you \nwill need to adjust them in the appropriate tickets.", "note": "She chases rates again the next month, and the desk has to fix tickets afterwards."},
    {"file": "corpus/farmer-d/logistics/867.eml", "quote": "Lauri's matrix shows 0.05 from Thompsonville \nto HSC, but the transport usage ticket (updated by Daren's group) has 0.055.", "note": "Rates keyed by hand drift away from the matrix. This is why accounting took on the refresh."},
    {"file": "corpus/farmer-d/logistics/867.eml", "quote": "The rates are in the system correctly in Unify (so that we can invoice \ncorrectly), but Daren's group uses a Sitara deal (the transport usage \ntickets) to estimate desk transport in the P&L during the month.", "note": "Correct rates already exist in the invoicing system. The tickets could take them from there instead of being keyed again."},
    {"file": "corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1796.eml", "quote": "they can only be set up for approx. 3 months at \na  time.", "note": "Sitara's span limit is why tickets have to be extended or recreated."},
    {"file": "corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2111.eml", "quote": "You can copy the old tickets or create new ones.", "note": "A year later tickets were still copied forward by hand, and some were missed."}

content.text:
I rejected this proposal because the same work is already saved. Item 11 in `decisions.md`, "Monthly set-up of HPL transport usage tickets", makes the same change (Sitara rolls each ticket into the next month and fills rates from the rate matrix, so staff key only the exceptions). It is saved at $53.55 a month and cites the same messages (1144, 1145, 1257, 1796, 867, 2109, 2111). No more research would change this: it is a duplicate, not a weak idea.

Before finding the duplicate, I checked the proposal against the mail. The idea holds up, but some of the claims needed fixing:

- **Rate drift is the past, not today.** The 0.055 versus 0.05 mismatch in 867 (March 2000) came from Daren's group keying the rates. That message led accounting to take over the refresh. By May, 1144 says "Rates have been updated to reflect current matrix rates". So the claim that the in-month P&L is wrong today overstates things. What is still missing each month is the baseload and third-party rates that traders agree.
- **"Takes more than a day" is a stretch.** Heidi sent 1144 at about 1:30 pm Houston time and was finished by about 8:30 the next morning. The job spans two days, but 6 hours is a guess at the high end.
- **The schedulers' saving has no support.** Nothing in the mail backs "5 schedulers × 15 min". Carrying last month's volumes forward also doesn't remove the schedulers' job of entering the real volumes for the new month.
- **1796 is a different job.** It is Sabrae Zajac setting up past tickets for Vastar/Big Thicket, not the monthly refresh. It is fair evidence of the roughly 3-month limit and nothing more.
- **How often is not stated.** No message says the refresh happens monthly. Counted from the mail, it happened three times between May 2000 and March 2001 (June, July, and the Midcon tickets in 2111), which is 0.18 a month. Even at about 220 minutes saved each time, `check` gives only about $56 a month, close to the saved item's figure. A monthly rate would need a message that says the tickets are redone every month.

Files:
- C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-8\proposals\transport-usage-ticket-rollover.json (my corrected version, checked but not saved)
- C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-8\proposals\transport-usage-ticket-rollover-reject.json (the rejection, recorded in decisions.md)

Proposal: Simplify the monthly Investor Relations "volumetric explanations" round. Today Business Analysis & Reporting (Misti Day) emails ~11 regional controllers each month to review the Statistical Database and email back explanations for every ±10% year/year, quarter/quarter and month/month change, then compiles the emails. Change: the Statistical Database itself flags the ±10% variances per region, shows the computed EOL vs. non-EOL share and the largest counterparty changes behind each variance, pre-fills last month's explanation, and lets the controller confirm/edit in the database; BA&R pulls the explanations from the database instead of from email.

TODAY / evidence:
- Monthly by request of IR, with a fixed short deadline: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1416.eml (Misti Day, 18 Sep 2000, "Wholesale Volumes - August", To 11 controllers: Bruce, Gossett, Keiser, Kelly, Etter, Scott, Louie, Baumbach, Confer, Leschber, Anderson; cc 5 traders): "It's that time again for the monthly and quarterly volumetric explanations!  The database for August is now ready for viewing." ; "Investor Relations requests that Business Analysis & Reporting provide monthly volumetric analysis for Wholesale Operations in addition to the quarterly analysis.  Please review the analysis for August 2000 and provide explanations for all material changes (+/- 10%) for the year/year, quarter/quarter, and month/month variances." ; "It is essential that the volumes be verified by commercial personnel." ; "Please forward your verification and explanations via e-mail to me by 10:00am Friday, September 22."
- Same request for May: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1210.eml (15 Jun 2000, "Wholesale Volumes"): identical text "It's that time again for the monthly and quarterly volumetric explanations!  The database for May is now ready for viewing."
- The explanations repeat month to month and are about drivers the data already holds: 1210.eml reply (Baumbach, Texas): "Texas has a 42% increase Year to Year, a 22% increase Qtr. to Qtr. and a 30% increase Mo. to Mo.  The Yr. to Yr. and Qtr to Qtr increases can be explained by an increase in EOL transactions and Entex taking more gas.  The Mo. to Mo. increase is attributable to increase EOL transactions and TUFCO taking more gas." ; 1416.eml reply three months later: "Yr to Yr and Qtr to Qtr changes due to EOL and increased Entex takes." (cc Daren Farmer, who is copied for verification each time).

CHANGE: (1) Statistical Database computes and displays, per region, the ±10% variances plus the EOL share change and top counterparty volume changes behind them (EOL vs non-EOL and counterparty are deal attributes already in the data). (2) Each flagged line shows last month's explanation, pre-filled; controller confirms or edits in an explanation field in the database. (3) BA&R exports the explanations for IR; no email collection.

AFTER: Controllers spend a few minutes confirming pre-filled, data-supported explanations; no separate email reply/cc chain; BA&R doesn't compile 11 emails.

ESTIMATE (monthly, stated in 1416.eml/1210.eml):
- Controllers: ~11 × (today ~15 min to open database, work out drivers, write and send email, cc the commercial verifier) → ~6 min confirm/edit = ~9 min saved each ≈ 100 min.
- Commercial verifier copied on reply (e.g., Farmer cc'd): ~11 × 2 min reading → 0 ≈ 20 min (verification can be done in the database view when needed; conservatively count 10 min).
- BA&R compiling ~11 emails into the IR analysis ~3 min each ≈ 33 min → ~5 min export = ~28 min.
- Total ≈ 138 min ≈ 2.3 h/month ≈ $196/month at $85/h.
